pl-l4d4c2-d1e115.summary: States that those who come without faith or insincerely receive the sacrament but not the reality.
claims: The insincere receive the sacrament without the reality.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e118.summary: Quotes Jerome: there are washings of gentiles and heretics, but they do not wash unto salvation; even in the Church those who receive baptism without full faith receive water, not the Spirit.
claims: Baptism without full faith gives water but not the Spirit.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e127.summary: Quotes Augustine: the sacraments were common to all the Jews, but not the grace that is their power; so now baptism is common to all the baptized, but not its power, which is grace.
claims: The sacrament is common to all the baptized; its grace is not.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e137.summary: Quotes Augustine: anyone who is master of his own will cannot begin a new life when he comes to the sacrament unless he repents of the old; only infants are exempt from this repentance when baptized.
claims: Adults must repent to begin new life in baptism.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e143.summary: Concludes that these testimonies show that adults without faith and true repentance do not receive the grace of remission in baptism, as infants do not receive remission without another's faith, since they cannot have their own. Whoever approaches insincerely, without true contrition of heart, receives the sacrament without the reality.
claims: Adults without faith and repentance do not receive remission.
Infants receive remission through the faith of others.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e146.summary: Notes that Augustine seems to say that to one who approaches insincerely, even harboring hatred of his brother, all is forgiven at the moment of baptism and returns at once afterward, but he says this comparing opinions, not asserting it. He writes that either sins are not forgiven to the insincere at all, or are forgiven by the power of the sacrament and return through insincerity, so that the holiness of baptism clothes him with Christ and the ruin of insincerity strips him; that forgiven sins return without fraternal charity is taught by the parable of the unforgiving servant.
claims: Augustine presents two opinions on whether the insincere are forgiven.
One opinion holds sins are forgiven at baptism and return through insincerity.
Lombard reads this as comparison of opinions, not Augustine's assertion.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e161.summary: Shows that Augustine did not assert this, since in the same book he says: if one comes insincerely to baptism, his sins are either forgiven or not; let them choose. So he spoke inquiring and reporting others' opinion.

pl-l4d4c2-d1e170.summary: Adds Augustine: baptism begins to avail for salvation when that insincerity withdraws by true confession, which, while the heart persisted in malice, did not allow the washing away of sins. So sins are not forgiven to one who approaches insincerely.
claims: Baptism begins to profit when insincerity is removed.
Sins are not forgiven to the insincere.

pl-l4d4c2.summary: Holds that those who come to baptism without faith or insincerely receive the sacrament without the reality. Jerome and Augustine: heretics' washings do not wash unto salvation; the sacrament is common to all the baptized, but not its grace; adults must repent of their old life. So adults without faith and true repentance do not receive remission, as infants do not without another's faith. Augustine seems to suggest that sins are forgiven to the insincere at the moment of baptism and then return, but he raised this as an opinion, not an assertion, letting readers choose; and he says baptism begins to profit only when the insincerity departs by true confession. So sins are not forgiven the insincere.
claims: Those who approach insincerely receive the sacrament without its reality.
Adults need faith and repentance to receive remission in baptism.
Infants receive remission through another's faith.
Augustine's view that sins return after baptism was tentative, not asserted.
Baptism begins to profit the insincere when insincerity is removed.
